$comment: Prioritised work. See engineering/README.md for priority and status conventions. Keep this deduplicated and honest — a backlog of a thousand generated items is a backlog nobody reads.

items.description: Bounded autonomous iteration, reachable from a real request: generate, review, decide, revise, generate again.
items.whyItMatters: RESOLVED. The loop was previously tested but unreachable — an orchestrated run generated once and reviewed once, so the autonomous-improvement behaviour the workspace could display could not actually occur.
acceptanceCriteria: A run whose review fails produces a second attempt without a new user request
The attempt ceiling is enforced inside the run, not only inside iterateWithReview
Every attempt persists as an ArtifactVersion with lineage, including rejected ones
items.verificationCriteria: An acceptance test where the first review fails and the second passes, asserting exactly two provider calls and two persisted versions.
items.designNote: The executor runs a flat ordered step list; it has no loop construct. Either the orchestrator appends a retry step when a review fails (needs the executor to support dynamic step insertion), or a single step owns the whole loop internally. The second is smaller and keeps the executor unchanged — decide deliberately.
items.implementation: One step owns the loop (capabilities/refine.ts), registered as media.image.refine at ACT. Rejected dynamic step insertion because step references are keyed by step ORDER and insertion silently repoints them. Loop position recovers from append-only ArtifactVersions carrying parameters.attempt, so an interrupted run does not re-pay for generation. Revision directives (capabilities/revision.ts) carry CHANGE plus a derived PRESERVE list; the decision engine (capabilities/decide.ts) is pure and covers approve, iterate, ceiling, stalling, not-fixable-by-generation, provider-unavailable and execution-failure.
items.verification: 20 tests in tests/iteration-acceptance.test.ts, all starting at driveRequest with an English sentence. Tests A-H plus the brief's full sentence (three variations, compare, improve the winner, attach to the Suit Bay) and its negative case (a one-shot request stays one shot, one provider call). Provider-call counts asserted throughout, so the cost claims are measured rather than asserted. Full suite 712/712, typecheck clean, lint 0 errors. Workspace inspected as rendered at 1100px and 390px.
remainingLimitations: IMAGE only — no video equivalent, which would need frame sampling that does not exist.
Resume re-reviews an attempt that was generated but not yet reviewed (one extra review call). Generation is never repeated.

items.description: Poll submitted video jobs and close their CapabilityRun rows.
items.whyItMatters: submitVideo returns a job and leaves the CapabilityRun RUNNING forever. The trace therefore reports a run as permanently live, and no cost is ever recorded for video.
acceptanceCriteria: A completed provider job closes its CapabilityRun with status, duration and cost
A failed job records the failure reason
The trace stops reporting live once the job settles
items.verificationCriteria: Unit test with an injected video provider returning a terminal job status.

items.description: Route the chat entry point through the capability orchestrator so a conversational request can start a real run.
items.whyItMatters: RESOLVED. Chat terminated at a text response, so the main entry point could not do the main thing.
acceptanceCriteria: A chat message that routes to a non-empty plan starts a run and returns its id
A message that routes to an empty plan still answers normally, with no AgentRun created
The response links to the workspace for the run
items.verificationCriteria: Integration test covering both branches; assert no AgentRun row for an ordinary question.
items.implementation: One branch in POST /api/chat before the model call. decideChatAction() (src/lib/chat/action.ts) runs the existing deterministic router pass with no classifier — zero model calls to classify. An executable plan goes to driveRequest(); the reply is composed from the resulting trace, so the orchestrated path spends nothing on prose either. Streams on the SAME NDJSON protocol with one additive run_started frame, so an un-updated client still renders correctly.
items.verification: 17 tests in tests/chat-orchestration.test.ts calling the real route handler with a real Request. Tests A-H including permission denial, provider failure, resume, and asserted provider-call counts. Full suite 729/729. Real chat UI driven in a browser at 1100px and 390px.

items.description: Suit asset lifecycle: catalog -> preview -> selected -> hero, so 60+ suits do not each hold hero-resolution resources.
items.whyItMatters: Directive section 22. Without a promotion/demotion lifecycle, scaling the catalogue degrades memory and frame rate on exactly the devices that matter most.
acceptanceCriteria: Only the active suit holds hero-fidelity resources
Deselecting a suit disposes its GPU resources
Switching suits does not grow memory monotonically
items.verificationCriteria: Measured before/after: resident GPU memory and suit-switch time across ten switches. Numbers recorded, not asserted from intuition.

items.description: Hands: five-finger definition, thumb opposition, fingernail plates.
items.whyItMatters: Hands are the second thing a viewer looks at after the mask, and currently read as mittens at close camera distances.
acceptanceCriteria: Five separated digits
Thumb opposes rather than sitting in the finger plane
Nail plates read at hero camera distance
items.verificationCriteria: Render at hero distance and inspect the image. Blender (bpy 5.0.1) must be reinstalled in a fresh container: pip install bpy==5.0.1.
items.note: Recorded lesson from earlier passes: a feature only reads by CONTRAST with its surroundings — scaling every sculpt field up together produces pouches, not detail.

items.description: Garment and fabric micro-detail: seam pressure, panel transitions, roughness variation that reads as technical textile rather than armour.
items.whyItMatters: Directive section 16 — the design language is ADVANCED TECHNICAL FABRIC, not armoured sci-fi. This is the difference.
acceptanceCriteria: Fabric reads as woven at hero distance
No moiré at any supported camera distance
items.verificationCriteria: Render and inspect. Respect the Nyquist clamp already in texturing.py — weave period must stay above ~5 texels or it aliases.
items.note: Recorded lesson: never derive a texture feature from a texture-space gradient. Adjacent texels are metres apart across UV seams; derive in world space.

items.description: Deterministic repository scanner that reports findings into this backlog without calling any model.
items.whyItMatters: Directive sections 34-38 want a free engineering shift that uses zero inference. The value is in what it detects deterministically: oversized assets, missing responsive variants, undisposed 3D resources, bundle regressions.
acceptanceCriteria: Runs offline with no API key and no model call
Appends deduplicated items to backlog.json rather than rewriting it
Only auto-fixes changes that are deterministic, reversible and test-verified; everything else becomes a needsOpus item
items.verificationCriteria: Run twice in succession — the second run must add nothing new. A scanner that regenerates its own findings is noise.
items.constraint: MUST NOT circumvent Anthropic usage limits, impersonate Claude, or substitute another paid model. Deterministic tooling and genuinely local tools only.

items.description: Establish measured baselines: JS bundle, 3D payload, initial load, suit-switch time.
items.whyItMatters: Directive section 32 — improvements cannot be claimed without measurement, and there is currently no baseline to compare against.
acceptanceCriteria: Baseline numbers recorded in engineering/state.json
Reproducible command documented
items.verificationCriteria: Two consecutive measurements agree within a stated tolerance.

items.description: Persist per-attempt review state so resume does not re-review an attempt that was generated but not yet judged.
items.whyItMatters: The loop recovers generation (the expensive half) but not review. An interruption between generating and reviewing costs one extra vision call on resume. Small, but it is the one remaining place where recovery is not exact.
acceptanceCriteria: A resumed loop re-reviews nothing that was already reviewed
items.verificationCriteria: Interrupt between generation and review; assert the review call count on resume.

items.description: Make a chat-started run asynchronous: return immediately and stream progress from the event bus instead of holding the HTTP response open until the run finishes.
items.whyItMatters: RESOLVED. Chat held the HTTP response open for the whole run, so a multi-step workflow looked frozen and any proxy in between could kill the response while the run carried on unseen.
acceptanceCriteria: The chat response returns as soon as the run is created
Progress reaches the client over the existing event stream, not a second protocol
A dropped connection does not affect the run, and reopening the conversation shows current state
items.verificationCriteria: A test asserting the response closes before the run completes, and that the persisted message is later reconciled with the final outcome.
items.implementation: agents/service.ts split into createAgentRun (persist) and startAgentRun (persist + execute), so driveRequest({ background: true }) can return once the run is DURABLE and run executeRun off the response. No second orchestrator, no duplicated executor, no second event bus. The chat route persists its assistant message BEFORE the work with the runId in its meta — that message is the reconnection anchor — and rewrites it in place via chat/service.ts#updateAssistantMessage when the onSettled callback fires. components/chat/InlineRunProgress.tsx renders live state from the EXISTING SSE bus, refetching the trace only on agent./capability./artifact./iteration. events; there is no polling loop and no fabricated progress. The panel reports a terminal run on its first non-live read rather than on a live->settled transition, because a short run can settle before it mounts.
items.verification: 24 tests in tests/chat-orchestration.test.ts including a timing test that asserts the POST has returned while the run is still RUNNING. Full suite 736/736, typecheck clean, lint 0 errors. Browser-verified against a real logged-in session in a FRESH conversation (so no earlier panel could satisfy the wait): panel live at ~270-320ms, message rewritten to the real outcome at ~1.5s with no reload, exactly one panel and the outcome text recovered after a full reload, 0px overflow at 1100px and 390px. Cost: 0 additional model calls, 0 additional image-generation calls, 0 additional QA calls — the plan summary and the outcome text are both composed from persisted state.
remainingLimitations: The WAITING_FOR_PERMISSION rendering is covered by tests but was not photographed in a browser: in this environment every chat-reachable capability is either already granted to the QA user or has no configured provider, so no chat message could be made to park on permission.
Nothing pushes a notification when a background run finishes with the tab closed; the rewritten message is waiting on the next visit.
A run interrupted by a process restart is recoverable via resumeRun but nothing resumes it automatically.

items.description: Brain Visual Engine — deepen the shipping 3D Brain into a real interactive cognitive interface.
items.whyItMatters: The Brain is the product's centre and currently under-represents what VOX actually does: the capability orchestrator is invisible to it, there is no intensity signal, the cortex is a single shell, and signals ride an abstract web rather than anatomy.
items.complexity: high — 10 bounded phases (A-J), each independently verifiable
items.plan: BRAIN_VISUAL_ENGINE.md — read section 1 (reuse inventory) before writing code, then section 9.
acceptanceCriteria: Anatomy reads as a brain (two hemispheres, visible folding, distinct cerebellum and brainstem) at 390px and 1100px
Every visual state is reachable from a real recorded event, and no state is reachable without one
WAITING_FOR_PERMISSION is visually distinct from executing and from error; degraded is grey, error is red
Reduced motion keeps state colour and drops signal travel
No WebGL context leak across route changes
MOBILE tier holds 30fps at 390px with transmission and vascular layers off
items.verificationCriteria: brain-geometry/brain-visual-state/brain-event-coverage tests plus a browser state sweep (idle, thinking, executing, iterating, waiting, degraded, error, completed) at both viewports.
items.designNote: Do NOT create a second brain component tree, a client state library, a second event bus, or a BrainEngine class wrapper. Seven new files, listed in section 6. VoxBrain3D.tsx is already 684 lines — extract state into useBrainVisualState before adding to it.
items.startAt: Phase A (anatomical foundation): cortical depth layer + lobe submeshes in brainGeometry.ts, with brain-geometry.test.ts extended first. Phase C is now cheaper: useBrainVisualState is the seam and intensity.ts is its scalar — wire getBrainVisualState() in lib/brain/ to feed ActivitySnapshot from CapabilityRun/AgentRun rows.
preparationDone: GPU lifecycle audited — already correct; fixed per-frame Vector3 allocation in BrainMesh and EntitySatellite.
useBrainVisualState extracted: VoxBrain3D 684 -> 616 lines, domain/event state separated from view state.
lib/brain/intensity.ts — deterministic 0..1 activity scalar with 17 tests.
